title: The Future of Domestic Financing for Health is Now: Africa’s Pathway to Sustainable Health Systems
host: The Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage, Republic of Côte d’Ivoire, The Ministry of Health, Republic of South Africa, in collaboration with Global Fund
description: This event is organized by the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, under the leadership of Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, and co-hosted with the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, the African Union Commission (AUC), several regional partners, and the Global Fund.  It will bring together Ministers of Health and Finance, senior national policymakers, global and regional advocates for health financing, and development and donor partners. The objective is to foster dialogue on financial sustainability and the transition of African health sectors from donor dependency to increased domestic financing. It will also offer a platform for countries to share lessons, evidence-informed approaches, and strategies for maintaining essential health services and programs amid fiscal and geopolitical uncertainty.

title: Redefinition des priorites et desallocation du Fonds mondial: Qu'est-ce que cela veut dire et comment les communautes peuvent-elle se preparer et s'y engager

title: Webinar on the results of the 53rd meeting of the Global Fund's Board / Вебинар по результатам 53-го заседания Правления Глобального фонда
description:
The aim of the webinar – is to provide the civil society and communities representatives from EECA region with an opportunity to receive the first-hand information about key topics being discussed during this Board meeting, the decisions being made and discuss how these decisions could impact HIV and TB responses as well as availability of the Global Fund’s support for countries in our region. Additionally, participants will have an opportunity to address the representatives of at least three Delegations to the Global Fund Board with all the questions they might have.

Цель вебинара – предоставить представителям гражданского общества и сообществ из региона ВЕЦА возможность получить информацию из первых рук о ключевых темах и решениях, принятых на этом заседании, а также дать возможность понять, как эти решения могут повлиять на меры по борьбе с ВИЧ и туберкулезом, а также на доступность поддержки Глобального фонда для стран нашего региона. Кроме того, у участников будет возможность обратиться к представителям как минимум трех делегаций в Правлении Глобального фонда со всеми интересующими их вопросами.

description:

Are you involved in Global Fund processes?

Are you pushing back against hamrful cuts?

title: Webinar on the Global Fund, Digital Health and Human Rights
host: Developed Country NGO, Developing Country NGO and Communities Delegations
description:
The Global Fund spends over US$150 million annually to strengthen health information systems, improve the availability and quality of digital data, and provide digital tools for health workers, which leverages private sector partnerships to support its investments. The Developed Country NGO Delegation to the Global Fund Board commissioned a study to investigate the challenges that Global Fund communities and civil society experience in the digital health transformation, viewed from a rights-based perspective. The webinar will present recommendations based on the study, and we will hear from the Global Fund Secretariat and representatives from communities and civil society on how to move these issues forward. Please find the study and brief here.

We invite you to also sign on to this letter to the new Global Fund Committee Leadership to address the recommendations, including the development of a digital strategy under the joint mandate of the Strategy Committee and Audit and Finance Committee, at the upcoming Committee meetings in July.

title: Programmatic Efficiency: Private Sector Engagement in TB Care
description: Join us for a dynamic webinar on “Strategic Private Sector Engagement & Programmatic Efficiency in TB Care,” where global and country experts will share how TB programs are adapting to funding constraints by leveraging private-sector partnerships, digital tools, and innovative efficiency models. With insights from the latest Global Fund reports, hear how countries like Kenya, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Nigeria are sustaining and expanding TB care through smart integration of private providers and resource optimization. Learn about practical strategies for resilient, high-impact TB programming in a changing global landscape.

title: Innovative Finance Series #2: Debt2Health: From Theory to Action!
description: In this webinar, we will examine Debt2Health and debt swaps with our guest speaker Dr Syarifah Liza Munira, Senior Advisor at the Joep Lange Institute and Former Director General of the Health Policy Agency, Ministry of Health Indonesia. title: Quo vadis, Global Health?
description:
This one-hour discussion, part of the “Quo vadis, Global Health?” series, explores political and structural challenges to global health in times of geopolitical disruption. It aims to safeguard the Global Fund’s role in fragile contexts—particularly through a successful 8th Replenishment for 2026–2028.

We look forward to an engaging exchange with representatives of the community of people who use drugs, from humanitarian aid, and from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) to reflect on the approaches to strengthening health and community systems to ensure equitable access and continue saving lives.

title: Navigating the future: Transition & Sustainability of HIV, TB & Malaria Responses
host: MENA Learning Hub, Asia Pacific Learning Hub, Anglophone Africa Learning Hub, EECA Learning Hub, Francophone Africa Learning Hub, LAC Learning Hub
description:
Please join us to our Joint Learning Hub Webinar on Sustainability and Transition in HIV, TB and Malaria Responses.
The webinar aims to provide participants with an opportunity to reflect on several interconnected issues crucial for countries facing ongoing challenges, including:
* Making the business case for community responses
* Different stages of shared learning
* Exploring social contracting as a pathway
* Practical opportunities in Grant Cycle 8
language: English (translation available in Arabic, French, Russian, Spanish)

title: Pushing the Last Mile for Gender-Transformative Investments through the Global Fund's 8th Replenishment
description:
The time has come for the Global Fund's 8th Replenishment & its mission to save lives and defeat HIV, TB and malaria and protect the progress we've made for women, girls, and gender-diverse communities.
But today's overlapping crises of climate change, conflict, inequalities are putting that progress at risk.
Millions of lives, especially women & girls in all their diversity, depend on full funding.
We are at a turning point. We cannot stop now.

title: Community lessons from Global Fund processes and steps forward to grant cycle 8
host: INPUD, MPact, GATE, NSWP
description: As the Global Fund grant revision and reprioritization process nears conclusion, GATE, INPUD, MPACT and NSWP, in collaboration with GBGMC, are inviting key population and community-led organizations to a webinar to reflect on what has worked, what has been challenging and what are the next steps for grant cycle 8.

title: Accélérer et Intensifier le Dépistage de la TB en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre
description:
Joignez-vous au RAME et à DEC (Diagnostic Equity Consortium) pour une série en deux parties consacrée à l’Afrique centrale et de l’ouest sur l’évolution et les stratégies visant à accroître le diagnostic de la tuberculose dans ces régions et au-delà.

Lors de la deuxième session, nous nous pencherons sur le positionnement optimal des moyens de diagnostic de la tuberculose au sein des réseaux nationaux de dépistage afin d’atteindre un plus grand nombre de personnes. Nos experts discuteront de la meilleure façon de placer et de distribuer les outils de dépistage de la tuberculose, en tenant compte de leurs caractéristiques, des besoins du système de santé et des préférences des communautés.

title: Health Architecture Reimagined - Civil Society Organisations (HEAR CSO) Launch
host: WACI Health, UHC2030 CSEM, STOPAIDS, NCD Alliance, GFAN, GNP+, ITPC
description:
Developed in response to the impact of the current geopolitical and development finance crisis, and at a moment of unprecedented change, the HEAR CSO Consortium is coordinated by a diverse consortium of civil society and community networks and organisations including WACI Health, UHC2030 CSEM, STOPAIDS, NCD Alliance, GFAN, GNP+ and ITPC. We hope you will join us!

As last weeks UN General Assembly made clear, there is an urgent need to reimagine global health architecture to secure equitable, affordable and effective health care for all. HEAR CSO will create spaces for gathering and amplifying the voices of civil society and community leadership working across health issues and aspects of global health architecture, by which we mean the systems, structures, institutions, rules and processes that collectively guide, coordinate, finance and implement efforts to improve health on a global scale.

title: GFAN Call

title: Follow-Up Webinar on Community Engagement in USG Global Health and Countries MoU Negotiations
host: COMPASS, EANNASO, KP-TNC, Health Gap, Data Etc
description:
On 10th November 2025 a webinar was organized to provide civil society organizations, community advocates, and national stakeholders with a, deep-dive analysis of the draft USG MoUs and Companion Guide, highlighting three critical areas for urgent, country-level advocacy and amendment before the agreements are signed by mid-December. CSOs were also provided with negotiation tools and techniques to ensure the final MoUs are aligned with global targets, responsive to community needs, and focused on genuine public health impact, not just bilateral interests.

Initial intel within countries shows that negotiations are centered in Ministries of Finance, with limited participation from Ministries of Health and almost none from decentralized sub-national units, despite devolved governance in many countries. Senior USG officials are holding brief, highly selective meetings, leaving civil society and community networks outside the room. There is growing indication that USG may favor centralized national-treasury models, which could sideline local government delivery systems that have driven HIV gains. With MoUs expected to be finalized by 12 December 2025, the window for influence is becoming extremely narrow.

Following the 10 November 2025 webinar, participants requested a practical, country-focused follow-up session to share real-time intelligence across MoU countries and collectively strategize ways for communities to engage, even under highly constrained access.

title: Keeping Harm Reduction Alive: Strategies Amid a Global Funding Collapse
description:
Harm Reduction has been long underfunded. Harm Reduction International’s most recent findings show that harm reduction funding is meeting only 6% of the estimated necessary need in low- and middle-income countries. This research came before the United States pulled Official Development Assistance (ODA) funding through projects like PEPFAR, USAID, or pledges to the Global Fund. The situation we now face is undoubtedly more stark, with numerous low- and middle- income countries having been heavily reliant on US funding for harm reduction. Before this year, domestic funding for harm reduction had been decreasing, resulting in over-reliance on bilateral donations or international multilateral donors to fill the gap.

UNAIDS estimates that the permanent discontinuation of this important source of HIV funding will lead to an additional 6.6 million new HIV infections and 4.2 million AIDS-related deaths between 2025 and 2029. Amid this funding crisis we must re-assess our priorities and focus our efforts to retain vital and life-saving harm reduction services. The World Health Organization, along with The Global Fund, has stressed the importance of maintaining and sustaining the continuity of life-saving harm reduction interventions that are under threat. While the guidance is clear about the importance of maintaining these services for sustaining the life and health of people who use drugs - what does it mean for civil society advocacy?

The 2025 Update to the Global State of Harm Reduction allows us to take stock of major changes to harm reduction programming at the national level, providing general insights between editions of the more comprehensive biennial Global State. In the current context – the 2025 Update takes stock of the impact of these US funding cuts, giving us an initial overview of the countries most harshly hit, while highlighting the mitigating factors protecting other countries, such as in those with existing domestic funding for harm reduction

description:
Urgent: le Bureau de la sécurité sanitaire mondiale et de la diplomatie du Département d'État américain (GHSD) négocie actuellement des protocoles d'accord (POA) avec les gouvernements de dizaines de pays concernant le financement bilatéral de la lutte contre le VIH (via le programme PEPFAR) et des programmes de lutte contre la tuberculose, le paludisme, la poliomyélite et pour la santé maternelle et infantile.

Ces POAs prévoient d'importantes réductions budgétaires, dont les détails ne sont pas connus . La société civile ne fait pas partie des négociations, ce qui empêche toute reddition de comptes, à un moment où les coupes budgétaires désastreuses ont déjà fragilisé les programmes de prévention et de traitement. Un plaidoyer est nécessaire dans les pays francophones pour assurer la participation de la société civile . Rejoignez-nous pour en savoir plus sur les protocoles d'accord dans votre pays et pour élaborer ensemble des stratégies.

title: Women4GlobalFund 2025 Highlights of the Year Webinar
description:
2025 was a challenging year for gender equality and global health.

Severe funding cuts and a growing gender backlash are deeply concerning and we stand in solidarity with all those bearing the weight of this regressive wave.

In this context, our work together and the arenas where we could collaborate were fundamental to us and to our mission. We want to express our deep gratitude and our joy to be partners in advancing human rights, gender equality and the meaningful participation of women and girls in their diversity at the center of HIV, TB and malaria responses.

Amid shifting global dynamics, the 8th Replenishment process, and GC7 reprioritization, our collective work has been critical to safeguarding a Global Fund partnership to remain transformative, community & women led. The progress we have made together reflects a shared commitment that we must continue to protect and strengthen in the years ahead.

We are pleased to invite you to the Women4GlobalFund 2025 Highlights of the Year Webinar, where we will:

Share key achievements and milestones from 2025

Reflect on advocacy efforts during the 8th Replenishment and GC7 reprioritization

Discuss strategic priorities and focus areas for 2026

Explore opportunities to collaborate and advance our collective impact

title: Invitation à un webinaire sur l'intégration des agents de santé communautaires dans le système de santé
description:
Les décideurs politiques, les défenseurs de la santé publique et les praticiens ont appelé à une meilleure intégration des agents de santé communautaire (ASC) dans le système de santé en général et dans les soins de sant primaires en particulier. L'appel à l'action de Bangkok encourage les parties prenantes à soutenir l'intégration des soins de santé communautaires professionnels dans les systèmes de santé nationaux en tant que pratique standard, à garantir un soutien à long terme, à utiliser des technologies adaptée et à instaurer la confiance et l'inclusion dans les environnements fragiles afin de protéger les communautés et d'améliorer les résultats en matière de santé.
Dans ce webinaire, nous explorerons les conditions qui permettent la mise en place de mécanismes d'achat stratégique durables pour soutenir l'institutionnalisation des programmes d'ASC et la mise en œuvre de ces programmes, ainsi que les options possibles à cette fin. Les présentations des pays et la table ronde qui suivra porteront sur les expériences du Kenya et du Burkina Faso. Nous entendrons également le témoignage d'une défenseuse des agents de santé communautaire du Kenya.
La session se déroulera en anglais et sera interprétée simultanément en français. Elle sera interactive : vous pourrez poser vos questions aux panélistes.
Au plaisir de partager cette session avec vous!
L'équipe du webinaire

Agenda
* Introduction — Fouzia Shafique (UNICEF)
* Présentation de cadrage — Soleine Scotney (Financing Alliance for Health)
* Table ronde — Maureen Kimani (Ministère de la santé, Kenya) et Mahamadi Tassembedo (Ministère de la santé, Burkina Faso)
Facilitation: Maud Juquois (GFF)
* Porte-parole des agents de santé communautaire — Margaret Odera (Kenya)
* Session de questions/réponses
* Synthèse — Nicholas Oliphant (Fonds mondial)

title: HEAR CSO Update: Civil Society Priorities for Global Health Architecture Reform
description:
In 2026, governments, funders and international agencies will make decisions about how to change the institutions, financing flows and governance structures that shape global health. Unless civil society and diverse communities impacted by health inequities require it, not all voices will be heard, and not everyone will be in the room. Join the Health Architecture Reimagined Civil Society Organization Consortium (HEAR CSO) on January 22 at 09:00 EST, 14:00 GMT, 15:00 CET and SAT, 17:00 EAT for an important planning and update call.

You’ll hear about the key findings from our seven regional consultations that engaged more than 130 people from 54 countries and 107 organizations. (And if you haven’t already, please check out the summaries and synthesis from these consultations at hearcso.org)

We will share a working calendar of processes and decision points anticipated in 2026, identifying areas for potential civil society coordination and action.

title: What Could Go Right? Partnering with Communities and Civil Society for New TB Vaccines
description:
New tuberculosis (TB) vaccines could be realized as soon as 2028 — radically reshaping the journey to eliminate TB. Communities and civil society organizations are poised to play a vital role in the introduction of a future TB vaccine as central protagonists of this next chapter for TB elimination.

TAG’s forthcoming report, What Could Go Right? Vital Partnerships with Communities and Civil Society for New Tuberculosis Vaccines, explores the foundational role that community and civil society groups can play in the successful introduction of a new TB vaccine and strategies for capacitating and empowering communities towards that goal. In bringing together three unique sub-studies, this first-of-its-kind report examines community and civil society’s readiness to engage in TB vaccine advocacy and policymaking at national, regional, and global levels, and underscores the transformative role communities can play in TB vaccine introduction, as well as the critical need for other stakeholders to help them realize that potential.

Please join us to discuss What Could Go Right? Partnering with Communities and Civil Society for New TB Vaccine and the path forward to capacitating and engaging community and civil society in the preparation for and introduction of a future TB vaccine.

title: Unpacking Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) and Pandemic Preparedness and Response (PPR) in GC8: Through the Community Lens.
host: Asia Pacific Regional Learning Hub, Seven Alliance, MENA Learning Hub, Anglophone Africa Learning Hub, EECA Learning Hub, Francophone Africa Learning Hub, LAC Learning Hub
description:
Please join us for the Joint Learning Hub Webinar: Unpacking Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) and Pandemic Preparedness and Response (PPR) in GC8: Through the Community Lens.


Organized by the Asia Pacific Regional Learning Hub (APRLH) by Seven Alliance, in collaboration with MENA, Anglophone Africa, , EECA, Francophone Africa, and LAC Learning Hubs,, this session aims to build community capacity and ensure meaningful participation in Grant Cycle 8 (GC8) processes.


The webinar will cover:

- The RSSH-PPR Information Note from a community perspective.

- CRSS, human rights, and gender-related modules within the GC8 framework.

- Strategic entry points for community engagement in country dialogues.

- Community-friendly tools and guidance for GC8.
language: English (translation available in Arabic, French, Portuguese, Russian)
